title: Let’s talk about what it takes to craft a good mystery, and why I fee...
transcript: The receptionist is a psychological thriller of sorts in which a series of small, strange occurrences slowly snowball into something much larger. I'm going to be very vague when describing the plot of this show, because so much of this show is meant to be intentionally mysterious. It's very season one of lost, where it's constantly raising a bunch of questions, but not necessarily giving you a lot of answers. So if you are someone that really enjoys theorizing, then you're going to have a ton to unpack and talk about after the show. But if you are someone that prefers definitive endings and closure, then you may find this play frustrating. And unfortunately, I fell more in the latter category. I felt like this play did a really good job at building tension, but there's never really any payoff. It felt like it was building up to some kind of big reveal or twist that just never came. And despite the intrigue, nothing in this play truly surprised me. I will say the cast is excellent. Our titular receptionist is played by the always fantastic Katie Finneran. She basically never leaves the stage, and so, so much of this play rides on her performance, and I definitely think she is up to the task. The rest of the cast is great as well, including Mallori Johnson, who's about to start in the film adaptation of is god is? With Kara Young. And so, while she is definitely still early In her career, she's definitely one to watch. But I do feel like this cast is held back a bit by the material. It feels like they are constantly having to play into the mystery rather than actually play into their characters. And that's the problem with plays that don't really provide any answers to their mysteries. You have to withhold information about your character in order to make the mystery compelling. And when there's no reveal, that information stays withheld. And at the end of the day, the hardest part about crafting a good mystery is the solution. Coming up with something that feels surprising in the moment and yet so obvious in hindsight. And I can't help but feel that by not providing any solution, the playwright kind of took the easy way out here.
reasoning: Reviewer praises the cast but criticizes the play for building tension without payoff and accuses the playwright of taking 'the easy way out.' The overall signal discourages viewers who want closure.
